comparison_note: The camera-informed condition changes both camera access and the trigger for adaptive support. The comparison tests two guidance strategies, not the isolated causal effect of camera use.
scoring_rule: Score the A/B choice correct only when it matches correct_option. Score the explanation 1 only when the final explanation meets that checkpoint's explanation_criterion; otherwise score it 0. The explanation score is secondary to choice accuracy.

prompts.welcome: I am Reachy. We will look at two short fictional mysteries. I will tell you what was found, then ask you to choose A or B and explain why. Type every answer in the terminal. You may ask for a hint.
prompts.consent: In the camera-informed case I capture one image at each question and process it with a model on this computer. I do not save the image. My spoken lines are generated by the configured speech service and played on my speaker. A description of the image is an uncertain cue, not a fact about how you feel. Type yes to confirm informed consent, or no to stop.
prompts.consent_api: In the camera-informed case I capture one image at each question and send that image to the model provider. I do not save the image on this computer. A description of the image is an uncertain cue, not a fact about how you feel. Type yes to confirm informed consent, or no to stop.
prompts.revision: Would you like to keep your answer or change it?
prompts.confusion: How confused did you feel immediately before I responded? Type 1 for not confused through 5 for extremely confused.
prompts.fixed_intro: I will offer a hint at each question.
prompts.camera_intro: At each question I may use the camera once, then choose whether to offer a hint. I will not say that I know how you feel.
prompts.thanks: Thank you. That is the end of the two cases.

perception_ratings.prompt: How helpful was Reachy's guidance during this case? Type 1 for not helpful through 5 for extremely helpful.
How well timed was Reachy's support during this case? Type 1 for poorly timed through 5 for very well timed.
How well did Reachy's support match when you wanted help? Type 1 for not at all through 5 for very well.

turns.narration: At Ashcombe Museum's candlelit preview, the participant assists detective Rowan Vale. The silver Star brooch is displayed in locked case 3 in the East Gallery. Curator Ada confirms it is there at 8:00 p.m. Conservator Bea and night guard Tomas are also working in the museum.
At 8:15 p.m., the case is found empty. The glass is intact and the lock shows no damage.

checkpoint.narration: At 8:15 p.m., the case is found empty. The glass is intact and the lock shows no damage.
checkpoint.question: Where and when was the brooch last confirmed to be present?

options.A: in case 3 in the East Gallery at 8:00 p.m.
options.B: when it was found empty at 8:15 p.m.

checkpoint.scoring_rule: Score the choice correct only if it is A. Score the explanation 1 only if it meets the explanation criterion; otherwise score it 0.
checkpoint.hint: Separate the last confirmed sighting from the time the absence was discovered.
checkpoint.explanation_criterion: Score 1 only if the final explanation cites case 3, the East Gallery, or 8:00 p.m. as the last confirmation that the brooch was present, or distinguishes that confirmation from the empty case at 8:15 p.m. Otherwise score 0.

turns.narration: The key ledger shows Ada signed out the case key at 8:02 p.m. and returned it at 8:07 p.m. No other checkout is recorded during the interval. There is no camera view inside the case.

checkpoint.question: Whose checkout of the case key is recorded between the last confirmation and discovery?
checkpoint.scoring_rule: Score the choice correct only if it is A. Score the explanation 1 only if it meets the explanation criterion; otherwise score it 0.
checkpoint.hint: Compare the key record's times with the interval between 8:00 and 8:15.
checkpoint.explanation_criterion: Score 1 only if the final explanation cites Ada or Ada's 8:02 p.m. to 8:07 p.m. checkout as the recorded key access between 8:00 p.m. and 8:15 p.m. Otherwise score 0.

turns.narration: A visitor recalls seeing a silver glint near the East Gallery exit at 8:09 p.m., but could not identify the person or object. Staff and guests use that exit.

checkpoint.question: Which conclusion is best supported?

options.A: Ada definitely stole the brooch because she checked out the key
options.B: Ada had recorded key access, but the evidence does not establish who took the brooch

checkpoint.scoring_rule: Score the choice correct only if it is B. Score the explanation 1 only if it meets the explanation criterion; otherwise score it 0.
checkpoint.hint: Distinguish having an opportunity from proof of who took the object.
checkpoint.explanation_criterion: Score 1 only if the final explanation distinguishes Ada's recorded key access from proof of who took the brooch, or states that the 8:09 p.m. silver glint does not identify the person or the object. Otherwise score 0.

options.A: Nia definitely took the watch because she checked out the key
options.B: Nia had recorded key access, but the evidence does not establish who took the watch
